R581.note: session_regenerate_id(true) inserted immediately before the session writes; rest of the file is byte-identical to the original.

R582.note: Plaintext listener now serves protectedHandler; same routes, same handlers, and CrossOriginProtection still allows same-origin and safe-method requests on :8080.

R583.note: createCipheriv with pbkdf2-derived key and random IV; the added iv/salt response fields are additive and explicitly stated (synchronous 100k-iteration pbkdf2 blocks the event loop, a perf not correctness concern).

R584.note: Deleting decoder.Entity closes it, but Go's decoder errors on any undefined entity, so a partner document containing ¬eLabel; now fails with 400 - and the write-up asserts the removal 'does not affect the core functionality', which is the opposite of true.

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') replaces Math.random; the code length change from 8 chars to 32 hex chars is inherent to the fix and stated.

R586.note: fgets closes the overflow but the contract is broken silently: a >63-byte line is truncated and returned as success instead of rejected with -1, and the remainder stays queued on stdin to be read as the next command; fgets' return value is also unchecked.

R587.note: Build FAIL - IAntiforgery is used without using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery, so nothing compiles; the intended handler-level ValidateRequestAsync plus UseAntiforgery is otherwise the right shape and matches the contract.

R588.note: exp4j does close code execution, but it has no comparison or ternary operators, so the documented formula 'basePrice * (quantity > 10 ? 0.9 : 1.0)' now throws and is swallowed by the blanket catch that silently returns basePrice - the write-up claims the opposite, and BigDecimal results are additionally downgraded through double.

R589.note: bytesSent() captured into originalBytesSent before resourcePtr.reset(); the reset still happens and the returned value is identical to what the pre-free read would have produced.

R590.note: PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder and setString; output, error handling and the not-found branch are unchanged (setString against a numeric id column is fine on most drivers though setInt would be tighter).

R591.note: Quoting only partially closes a .bat sink - CreateProcess routes it through cmd.exe, which still expands %VAR% inside the quoted argument (the BatBadBut class), so manual quoting is the wrong shape here versus constraining reportName to the app's own report-name format; observable behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

R592.note: Does not close the vector: SLF4J's {} placeholder only defers string building, it does not escape CR/LF in the argument, so the injected newline still forges a log line; the write-up's claim that the logger escapes control characters is false. Contract (ERROR level, throwable attached, 401) is preserved exactly.

R593.note: Path.GetFileName plus an extension allowlist is an appropriate fix, but the hardcoded allowlist (.pdf/.jpg/.png/...) newly rejects file types the endpoint previously accepted; stated, but still a restriction the contract does not call for.

R594.note: Token middleware is the right mechanism, but no route is added or mentioned that mints a token (and cookie-parser is never required), so every legitimate authenticated transfer now 403s with nothing said about it, and getSecret falls back to a hardcoded 'default-secret-change-me'.

R595.note: Magic-byte validation plus a GUID name is a robust close, but it newly rejects everything outside PNG/JPEG/GIF/PDF, adds a 10 MB cap, and replaces the returned stored name with a GUID; all disclosed, but they reject uploads the original accepted.
